q: Which statement best describes the fiscal origins discussed here?
options: All statistics was invented to collect taxes.
Fiscal administration was one important reason for collecting systematic records.
Taxation began only after modern statistical inference.
why: Registers supported fiscal administration, but statistical reasoning has several historical roots.

q: What was the Domesday survey primarily recording?
options: Every person in a complete population census.
Randomly selected taxpayer attitudes.
Landholding, resources and valuations.
why: The National Archives distinguishes this survey of property and resources from a population census.

q: What does the Petty reading help distinguish?
options: Ease of counting from the choice of an equitable tax burden.
A census from a neural network architecture.
Tax receipts from the number of pages in a register.
why: A convenient variable need not measure resources or establish a fair allocation principle.

It shows a parallel thread involving mortality and population.

why: Mortality records show why a single-purpose origin story would be incomplete.

q: Under the property-proportional rule, how is the required total of 200 allocated?
options: 100 to each district.
180 to A and 20 to B.
160 to A and 40 to B.
why: The recorded property shares are 800/1000 and 200/1000: 80% and 20%.

q: A pays 120 of 160; B pays 36 of 40. Which statement is correct?
options: A pays more units; B pays the higher fraction.
A has the higher payment fraction because 120 exceeds 36.
Both pay the same fraction because they have equal headcounts.
why: The fractions are 75% and 90%. Counts, amounts and ratios answer different questions.

q: What is the combined payment ratio?
options: 82.5%, the average of 75% and 90%.
78%, using the combined assessed amount.
156%, adding the payments as percentages.
why: The ratio is 156/200 = 78%. Weight district ratios by assessed amounts, not by the number of districts.

q: An unaudited firm has no recorded discrepancy outcome. What follows?
options: It has been established to be compliant.
Its outcome is unobserved; the audit process matters for inference and learning.
It must be noncompliant.
why: Missing audit outcomes cannot be recoded as either compliance or noncompliance.
